sections.h2: Visiting the Manitowoc County Register of Deeds
sections.html:
The office is on the first floor of the Manitowoc courthouse, Room 107, at 1010 S 8th Street, Manitowoc, WI 54220. County deeds, mortgages and satisfactions all get filed here, and staff keep the permanent index.

Counter hours: Monday 8:30 to 5:00, Tuesday through Friday 8:30 to 4:30. Filing is accepted daily from 8:30 AM to 4:00 PM, so arrive early in the afternoon at the latest. Questions go to 920-683-4660.

Employees can't write a deed for you or offer legal opinions. Inherited homes, land contracts and clouded titles belong with a Wisconsin attorney or your closing title company before anything reaches the counter.

Manitowoc County counted 81,359 residents in 2020, with an estimate of 81,710 for July 2025. About 24.8 percent of residents are 65 or older, so many listings start with a family handling a parent's house. The county holds 38,298 housing units, 77.1 percent of them owner-occupied. The median owner-occupied home is worth $186,900, and median gross rent is $797 monthly.

At these prices the recording charge and transfer fee are minor beside what you spend on repairs or carrying the house. The filing steps don't change whether the house is worth $90,000 or $400,000.

Each deed you record costs $30, paid up front. Pulling a copy of anything on file costs $2 for the first sheet and $1 for each sheet after, with a $1 surcharge if you want it certified. State law fixes these base charges for all Wisconsin counties.

ChargeAmount
Deed or mortgage recording$30 per document
Copy of a filed document$2 first page, $1 per added page
Certification of a copy$1 extra
Subdivision or condominium plat$50
State transfer fee on a sale30 cents per $100 of value

Search and special handling charges are set by the office itself. Ask for the current schedule if you need either one.

sections.h2: How the state transfer fee works
sections.html:
The grantor, meaning the seller, pays this charge: 30 cents on every $100 of value, with any leftover fraction counted as a full $100 (Wis. Stat. 77.22). Payment is collected as the deed comes in, and the amount is marked on the deed face. Of each dollar collected, twenty cents stays in the county and the rest is forwarded to the state.

The clerk won't audit your stated price. By statute the register need not work out true value or test an exemption claim, so accuracy rests with whoever signs the return.

Certain transfers owe nothing. Section 77.25 exempts, among others:

  • Property passing through a will, descent or survivorship.
  • Family transfers for little or no payment, such as parent to child or grandparent to grandchild.
  • Land and buildings worth no more than $1,000.
  • A foreclosure deed or deed in lieu, when the grantee is the lender or land contract vendor.
  • Conveyances that come out of a delinquent tax or assessment sale.

An exempt deed must carry the matching subsection of 77.25 on its face.

Wis. Stat. 59.43(2m) lets the office bounce any instrument that departs from the standard layout. Here is what it looks for:

  • The title goes on page one, somewhere from 0.5 inch to 6 inches down from the top.
  • Reserve a square 3 inches on each side in the page one top right corner, because the stamp goes there.
  • Paper copies need return information on page one. E-filed ones don't.
  • The sheets should be white, at least 20 pound stock, 8.5 inches wide and either 11 or 14 inches long.
  • Ink must be black, blue or red, and sheets can't be hinged or joined on the top or sides.
  • Say who drafted the instrument.
  • Write or type the names of the grantor, the grantee and any notary so they can be read.

Keep Social Security numbers off the document entirely, because subsection (1m) bars recording one that shows it. A packet sent in as a single transaction can be returned whole if just one piece breaks the layout rules.

sections.h2: Can a deed be e-recorded here?
sections.html:
It can. Four vendors are named by the county, and you enroll with each separately: Simplifile (713-210-4323), Hopdox (385-501-5103), Indecomm (651-765-6400) and EPN (888-325-3365). If a title company or closing attorney runs your sale, expect them to use one.

A Wisconsin Electronic Real Estate Transfer Return (ERETR) is required for every deed too. Save it before you press submit, then print the receipt. That receipt has to accompany the original deed at the counter, and closing the page without printing means starting the return over.

The office runs a free alert service worth joining. A notice reaches you each time something is filed under your name or on your parcel, so you can verify it. The county calls real estate fraud uncommon in Wisconsin, and enrollment is a single call to 920-683-4660.

Alerts pay off for absentee owners, vacant inherited houses and anyone mid-sale. Once your own deed is filed, the same alert watches for anything recorded later, and that is useful peace of mind after closing.

sections.h2: Order of steps on a sale
sections.html: Closings here follow a set sequence. First the seller signs a deed laid out to the rules above. Someone files the electronic transfer return, usually the closing agent, and prints the receipt. The deed and receipt then go to the counter or through an e-recording vendor, with the $30 fee and any transfer fee paid. Last, the register stamps the document and adds it to the permanent index. A buyer paying cash skips the lender's mortgage, so there is one less document to record, but the deed and return are still needed. Ask for a copy of the filed deed afterward, since certified copies cost only $1 extra.

Run through a few things so you only make one trip. Compare the deed with the layout points above and confirm no Social Security number appears. Complete the electronic transfer return and print its receipt. Bring the $30 recording fee, and the transfer fee too unless the deed cites a 77.25 exemption. A title company closing your sale normally takes care of this; so does the closing agent for a cash buyer. If a detail on your document puzzles you, phone 920-683-4660 first.

faqs.q: Where is the Manitowoc County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: The office is in the courthouse at 1010 S 8th Street, 1st Floor, Room 107, Manitowoc, WI 54220. The phone is 920-683-4660. Recording runs daily from 8:30 AM to 4:00 PM.

faqs.q: What does recording a deed cost here?
faqs.a: Recording is $30 per document, paid in advance. A non-exempt sale also owes the state transfer fee of 30 cents per $100 of value. A copy is $2 for its first page and $1 per extra page, and $1 more certifies it.

faqs.q: Is anything filed with the state before recording?
faqs.a: Yes. File the Wisconsin Electronic Real Estate Transfer Return and print the receipt, which goes with the original deed. Only conveyances exempt under Wis. Stat. 77.25(1) or (10m) skip it.

faqs.q: Does passing down an inherited house owe the transfer fee?
faqs.a: Typically no. Transfers by will, descent or survivorship are exempt under Wis. Stat. 77.25(11). If the heir then sells to a buyer, that second conveyance carries the fee based on the price.

faqs.q: Can I use e-recording in Manitowoc County?
faqs.a: Yes, through Simplifile, Hopdox, Indecomm or EPN. Each handles its own enrollment by phone. Whoever runs your closing can say if they will file the deed this way.
